compressed_items.content: CGET is presented as a developing theoretical research framework for executable causal compression, controllable future reach, invariant preservation, alignment and self-modification.
Repository-level and layer-level status statements preserve theoretical/proposal/open/in-progress standing and explicitly separate completed formalization from unperformed measured validation.

Roadmap/future-direction items include toy validation, representation transfer, self-modification, value learning, alignment, larger systems, tool extensions and empirical measurement; direction is not completion or authority.

Open problems retain rigorous definition, causal/value closure measurement, core identity discovery, transition/agency metrics, tractability, empirical validation, biological/AGI relations, consciousness and mathematical existence/bound questions.

Explicit assumptions cover compressible reality, causal/executable representations, closure, viability, identity, timescale separation, agency/control, alignment, self-modification, structured future space and falsifiability.
Twelve axioms and master axiom define conceptual commitments; source explicitly denies complete/proven mathematical-theory standing.
Central hypothesis family proposes intelligence as executable causal compression plus controllable future expansion under invariant-preserving self-modification.

Specialized hypotheses concern closure, executability, identity preservation, alignment integration, viability-bound recursion, representation advantage over scaling and analyzer structural signatures.

Predictions cover representation-first capability, executability, controllable agency, identity-preserving self-improvement, value closure, viability, representation-vs-scale, CGET-vs-baseline ordering and expected transformation signatures.

Conceptual principles include dual epistemic/normative compression, non-compensable lexicographic constraints, conserved transformation, agency/viability distinctions, alignment internality and architecture/failure-mode interpretations.

Historical/cross-domain analyses and existing-work relationships are retained as source interpretations, including physics, AD, compilers, alpha-beta, AlphaZero, evolution, LLMs and conceptual relations to external fields.

Core vocabulary includes X,Z,B,Omega,rho,G,O/V, core/adaptive values, policies, reachable/steerable futures, A_control, self-modification T, viability/agency kernels and related source-local definitions.
Specialized definitions include interventional equivalence, closure/fidelity/leverage, identity/core-loss, transition stability, Theta*, Psi_stable, analyzer metric names and local notation.

Formal structures define coupled epistemic/normative state, executable causal language, constrained/lexicographic objective, kernels, closure, agency, identity and self-modification equations; source explicitly says equations are not assumed proven.

Architecture/protocol specifications cover epistemic/normative engines, analyzer data models/modules, benchmark pipelines and toy-agent experimental designs without implying implementation or execution.
Experimental/falsification methods define baseline comparisons, representation/intervention tests, agency/closure/self-modification evaluations, metric collection and benchmark constraints.
Example benchmark report contains synthetic configuration and numeric tables explicitly disclaimed as experimental results.

tools/experiments/test_results.md uses Result/Current Findings/CGET Classification labels for qualitative retrospective analyses of AD, compilers and alpha-beta. Source status is Initial Analysis; no execution provenance or measured instrument output is present.

No measured execution result or persisted benchmark execution record was observed on the exhaustive frozen surface. This does not negate source-labeled qualitative analyses and is not a global absence claim.
No reported negative execution result was observed on the frozen source surface; falsification conditions are prospective methods, not negative results.
Seven .py paths are stored literally inside Markdown code fences; extension does not establish executable Python blob standing.
Three analyzer files are ordinary Python source implementing toy metric arithmetic, hard-coded toy agents and a synthetic evaluation calculator.
Fenced experiment/agent/environment/metric/runner files contain intended implementation logic but are not directly executable as frozen blobs.

Implementation choices include hard-coded structural metric constants, manually assigned toy-agent fields, scalar proxy formulas, bounded Maze approximations and benchmark configuration/interface assumptions.
Several code artifacts contain intended direct-run printing/report/ranking behavior; no stored execution record licenses treating those outputs as observed.

Component code is present, but integrated environmental benchmark executability is not established: main runner is fenced and targets incompatible MazeWorld/agent interfaces; analyzer benchmark runner is also fenced.
CGET expands as Equilibrium, Execution and Executable Theory across source files; canonical expansion is not established.

Analyzer/benchmark documentation rejects or de-emphasizes a single scalar score and specifies lexicographic constraints, while run_benchmark.py intends to rank toy agents by Theta*. Reconciliation authority NONE.
Synthetic example_run explicitly denies result standing while test_results uses result/finding labels for Initial Analysis without execution provenance; both source-relative standings are preserved.
Ordinary executable components coexist with fenced .py artifacts and an interface-inconsistent intended environmental runner; component executability does not resolve integration executability.
References to external research fields/frameworks remain source-side conceptual references with no exact literature endpoint resolution and no Program Map edge effect.
